Get started

Source: vignettes/get-started.qmd

In a few minutes you’ll have a feature file written in plain language, steps in R that check it, and a run that tells you which scenarios pass. New to the idea behind it? Read vignette("bdd") first, or come back to it later.

Install 

install.packages("cucumber")

cucumber runs on testthat, so you need it too: install.packages("testthat").

Write a feature

A feature file describes behavior in Gherkin, one example per scenario. Each step is a line that starts with Given, When or Then. Save this as tests/acceptance/addition.feature:

Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding 2 integers
    When I add 1 and 1
    Then the result is 2
  Scenario: Adding integer and float
    When I add 1 and 1.1
    Then the result is 2.1
  Scenario: Adding float and float
    When I add 1.1 and 1.1
    Then the result is 2.2

Nothing in it says how to add numbers. That’s the point: the feature reads the same to someone who doesn’t write R.

Write the steps

A step definition connects a step’s text to R code. Save this as tests/acceptance/setup-steps-addition.R:

when("I add {float} and {float}", function(x, y, context) {
  context$result <- x + y
})

then("the result is {float}", function(expected, context) {
  expect_equal(context$result, expected)
})
  • "I add {float} and {float}" matches the text of a step. Each placeholder takes a number out of the text and passes it to the function, as x and y.
  • context is an environment the steps of one scenario share. The when step stores the result in it and the then step reads it.
  • expect_equal() is the testthat expectation you already know.

Run it

cucumber::test() runs the feature files of tests/acceptance:

  |  F  P  U  S  OK | Feature
✔ |               3 | Addition

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Summary
  3 scenarios (3 passed)
  6 steps (6 passed)
  0m00.067s (executing steps: 0m00.009s)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

One line per feature, with its scenarios counted by status. All three scenarios passed.

See a failure

Change the expected result in a Then step, say to 5, and run again. The reporter shows the step that failed, in which scenario, where its definition is, and how the values differ:

  |  F  P  U  S  OK | Feature

Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding 2 integers
    ✔ When I add 1 and 1
    ✖ Then the result is 5
    Error:
      Step "the result is 5" failed
      ℹ Feature: addition.feature:4
      ℹ Scenario: Adding 2 integers
      ℹ Step defined at: setup-steps-addition.R:5
      Expected `context$result` to equal `expected`.
      Differences:
      1/1 mismatches
      [1] 2 - 5 == -3
✖ |  1            2 | Addition

Failures:

1) Scenario: Adding 2 integers # addition.feature:2
    ✔ When I add 1 and 1
    ✖ Then the result is 5
    Error:
      Step "the result is 5" failed
      ℹ Feature: addition.feature:4
      ℹ Scenario: Adding 2 integers
      ℹ Step defined at: setup-steps-addition.R:5
      Expected `context$result` to equal `expected`.
      Differences:
      1/1 mismatches
      [1] 2 - 5 == -3

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Summary
  3 scenarios (1 failed, 2 passed)
  6 steps (1 failed, 5 passed)
  0m00.060s (executing steps: 0m00.028s)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Error: Test failures.

See every step

CucumberPrettyReporter prints each step as it runs, in color in a terminal:

Feature: Addition
  Scenario: Adding 2 integers
    ✔ When I add 1 and 1
    ✔ Then the result is 2
  Scenario: Adding integer and float
    ✔ When I add 1 and 1.1
    ✔ Then the result is 2.1
  Scenario: Adding float and float
    ✔ When I add 1.1 and 1.1
    ✔ Then the result is 2.2


────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Summary
  3 scenarios (3 passed)
  6 steps (6 passed)
  0m00.050s (executing steps: 0m00.010s)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CucumberDotsReporter, CucumberProgressBarReporter and CucumberSummaryReporter are the other console reporters. See the reference.

Where the files go

Keep acceptance tests apart from your unit tests:

tests/
├── acceptance/
│   ├── setup-steps_1.R
│   ├── setup-steps_2.R
│   ├── feature_1.feature
│   └── feature_2.feature
└── testthat/
    └── test-unit_test_1.R

or alongside them, and run the features from a testthat file with cucumber::run():

tests/
└── testthat/
    ├── test-cucumber.R
    ├── test-unit_test_1.R
    ├── setup-steps_1.R
    └── feature_1.feature

vignette("testthat") explains how the two ways differ.
